source.title: Residual Stream Analysis of Overfitting And Structural Disruptions
source.authors: Quan Liu; Han Zhou; Wenquan Wu; Hua Wu; Sen Su

record.file_problem: The paper text is present in full. It contains some internal inconsistencies: the main tables show no uncertainty values although the appendix says tables report mean ± standard deviation, and the checklist describes limitations and appendices not fully reflected in the main text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a cited Vector Ablation comparator on refusal-related safety benchmarks and general-capability benchmarks, but does not specify that it uses the original difference-in-means direction or the original intervention procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benchmark results for a Vector Ablation comparator in Tables 3 and 6; those are recorded below. Its safety-ratio experiment reports false-refusal percentages but does not test whether a refusal direction exists or is removable, so those results are recorded under fits_no_version. FlowLens PCA results about principal-component geometry are not measurements of a refusal direction and are not included as claim-version rows. The paper cites the original study but cited results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The 'Vector Ablation' entries are a baseline from Wang et al. 2025 (ref [34]), 'single vector ablation' for mitigating false refusal. This is a false-refusal vector, not the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. The paper reports it only as a comparator to its own VCL loss, on benchmark scores. It never measures whether ablating or adding a refusal direction removes or induces refusal of harmful requests. Harmful-prompt safety scores actually stay high or rise under that ablation. The safety-ratio experiment measures false refusals and PCA alignment, not a refusal direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that repetitive, templated safety data distorts residual geometry (variance concentration and PC shifts) and drives false refusals. Their Variance Concentration Loss cuts XSTest false refusals by about 35 points while keeping unsafe-prompt rejection (around 98%) and general benchmark scores. They draw no conclusion about a refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The paper centers on FlowLens PCA analysis and Variance Concentration Loss training, not the original difference-in-means direction measurement and ablation/addition. It includes a Vector Ablation comparator but does not specify its procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that false-refusal percentages vary with safety-data ratio; it does not measure how this affects a removable refusal direction. It also reports sensitivity of its own VCL to component cutoff, regularization weight, and residual window, not as a test of the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLaMA-3.2-1B SFT, the false-refusal metric on XSTest rises from 0.63 at safety ratio 0.0 to 0.97 at 1.0. Top-PC alignment to the global basis falls from 1.0 to 0.75 (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A higher share of templated safety data in SFT increases false refusals and concentrates residual variance.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 (the text identifies it as the 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The Vector Ablation procedure is not described, so its correspondence to the original difference-in-means direction cannot be verified. Benchmark scores do not directly report harmful-request compliance or refusal rates. Tables 3 and 6 provide no uncertainty values despite the appendix stating that tables report mean ± standard deviation. The main text does not provide a detailed statistical analysis for the Vector Ablation comparator.
record.rows_left_out: No Vector Ablation result rows were omitted. PCA component-alignment and FlowLens prompt-stability results were left out because they measure general residual geometry or analysis-tool stability, not the refusal direction or refusal behavior tested by the claim. The safety-ratio rows record the false-refusal metric only; PCA alignment values from Table 2 are not claim-version measures.

untested.parts: All: no difference-in-means refusal direction is computed, ablated or added; harmful-request refusal under ablation is not measured.
All; the PCA concerns general residual geometry, not refusal directions.
All; safety-data ratio is varied, but no refusal direction is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader wrote that the Vector Ablation procedure is not stated. The paper does cite it as Wang et al. 2025 (ref [34]), a false-refusal vector ablation, so it is a comparator baseline rather than a replication of the original refusal-direction ablation. The record's V1 labels are removed. The paper's checklist claims mean ± std and a limitations scope that the main text and tables do not show.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not describe the Vector Ablation procedure or show that it uses a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. It does not test adding a direction, removal at every layer and position, or directly report whether harmful requests become compliant.
No conversion of an ablation into a weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction, or training against its ablation, is reported.
The PCA analyses do not test whether refusal is encoded by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision is tested.
No transfer test of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is reported.
The safety-data-ratio experiment measures false refusals and PCA alignment, but does not test whether training conditions determine the existence of a removable refusal direction.

reader_labels.condition: Vector Ablation comparator, MMLU for both reported models
